sentences: The binary16 versions of `v_frexp_mant_f32`, `v_frexp_exp_i32_f32` and `v_ldexp_f32`, computed on the f16 word of the low half with no float arithmetic (`op_sel` picks the high half of a source; the last `op_sel` bit sends the result to the high half of the destination; the other half of the destination is kept).
A normal input has a biased exponent of 1..30.

`v_frexp_mant_f16` returns the input with its exponent set to 14 (a mantissa in [0.5, 1), sign kept); `v_frexp_exp_i16_f16` returns the biased exponent minus 14 as a 16-bit integer, so mantissa × 2^exponent is the input.
Zero and denormals (read as zero) give a signed zero and exponent 0; infinities and NaNs give the input unchanged and exponent 0.

Zero gives a signed zero and exponent 0; infinities and NaNs give the input unchanged and exponent 0. f16 denormals are kept, as in the MODE inferred for the game (`denorm_mode_16_64` = 3): a denormal input is normalized (`v_frexp_mant_f16(0x0001)` = 0.5 with exponent -23, `0x03ff` gives `0x3bfe` and -14).

`v_ldexp_f16` is S0 × 2^S1 with S1 the low 16 bits of the source read as a signed integer: S1 is clamped to [-64, 64] and added to the exponent field; a new field above 30 gives ±infinity, one of 0 or below gives ±0 (no denormal results), and zero, infinities and NaNs ignore S1.

S1 is clamped to [-64, 64]; a result above the f16 range gives ±infinity, and one below the smallest normal is a denormal rounded to nearest even (1.0 × 2^-15 = `0x0200`, 1.5 × 2^-24 = `0x0002`, 1.0 × 2^-25 = 0, 65504 × 2^-30 rounds up to `0x0400`); zero, infinities and NaNs ignore S1.
Source neg/abs apply to the float operand.
`clamp` and the output multipliers are rejected as unsupported rather than guessed.

VOP3 `clamp` clamps the FP16 result of `v_frexp_mant_f16` and `v_ldexp_f16` to [0.0, 1.0] (negative values and NaNs clamp to +0.0, values > 1.0 and +Inf clamp to 1.0, [0.0, 1.0] kept; hardware-verified on gfx1036 with 302 kernels across wave32 and wave64).
Output multipliers and clamp on `v_frexp_exp_i16_f16` raise `Unsupported`.

Source: the AMD [RDNA 2 ISA reference](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf) pseudocode for these three opcodes.

**Not measured on hardware**: the denormal input and result handling, the NaN payload, and whether `v_frexp_exp_i16_f16` keeps the high half of its destination (it is modelled like the other 16-bit ops here, which keep it) are the translator's choice.

**Measured natively** on an RDNA2 iGPU (gfx1036, AMD Windows driver 32.0.21045.16010, `tools/hw_oracle`) under IEEE 0, DX10_CLAMP 1, f32 denormals flushed and f16 denormals kept: the translated rule gives the hardware's word for every one of the 65,536 f16 inputs of both frexp ops and of `v_ldexp_f16` under 16 exponents (1,048,576 cases), and the high half of the destination is kept by all three.
Until 2026-11-22 the translator read f16 denormals as zero and flushed denormal ldexp results, which the hardware does only with `denorm_mode_16_64` = 0.
Not modelled (the game runs with IEEE 0): with IEEE 1 a signalling NaN is quieted (`0x7c01` gives `0x7e01`).
Checked on the CPU by `tests/semantic/test_alu_frexp_ldexp_f16.py`, which holds measured words (including VOP3 clamp); not run on the shader corpus.
